paper_metadata.title: Vacancy mediated alloying strengthening effects on γ/γ′ interface of Ni-based single crystal superalloys: A first-principles study

evidence.quote: Vacancy mediated alloying strengthening effects on γ/γ' interface of Ni-based single crystal superalloys: A first-principles study

The influences of vacancy on the site preferences and strengthening effects of alloying elements (Re, Mo, Ta, Cr) on the γ/γ' interface in Ni-based single crystal superalloys have been systematically studied by first-principles calculations.

conflicts.description: The source mentions that Wang [16] concluded γ'-Al is the most stable substitution site, whereas the present work finds γ-cpNi is the most preferable for Re, Mo, Ta, with Cr preferring the Ni vacancy site.

evidence.section: 3.1 Site preferences of alloying elements at γ/γ' interface
evidence.quote: Whereas in another work of γ/γ' interface by Wang [16], the Ni sites on (001) γ plane were not considered, which led them to the conclusion that γ'-Al was the most energetically stable substitution site.
